content.value_statement: Security work often needs structured checks across architecture, implementation, and testing. This skill provides local scripts and concise references for guided reviews.
actual_capabilities: Runs three local Python helper scripts for threat modeling, security auditing, and penetration-test planning.
Produces terminal reports and optional JSON output files when requested.
Provides reference pages for security architecture, penetration testing, and cryptography implementation.
Guides setup, quality checks, and common development commands.
Frames reviews around input validation, authentication, authorization, and data protection.
limitations: The included reference documents are generic templates, not deep expert playbooks.
The Python scripts currently generate placeholder findings unless extended by the user.
Penetration testing guidance requires explicit authorization and defined scope.
It does not replace manual security review, legal review, or compliance certification.

use_cases.title: Application Security Review
use_cases.description: Review a project structure, gather basic findings, and prepare a concise security report.

use_cases.title: Threat Model Workshop
use_cases.description: Create a structured threat model for a new service or major feature.

use_cases.title: Authorized Test Planning
use_cases.description: Plan a scoped penetration-test workflow with clear boundaries and reporting expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Review Security Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my project for basic application security issues. Summarize risks, likely causes, and practical next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Threat Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a threat model for this feature. Identify assets, trust boundaries, threats, controls, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Authorized Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan an authorized penetration test. Include scope, rules of engagement, test areas, evidence handling, and report format.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Architecture Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to evaluate this architecture for security risk. Prioritize findings by impact, exploitability, control gaps, and remediation effort.

output_examples.input: Review a small web service for security concerns.
output_examples.output: A short report listing target context, review status, finding count, key concerns, and recommended follow-up checks.

output_examples.input: Create a threat model for a payment feature.
output: Assets and trust boundaries are identified.
Threats are grouped by authentication, data flow, storage, and operations.
Mitigations and open questions are listed for engineering review.

output_examples.output: A scoped plan covering permitted targets, excluded actions, test phases, evidence handling, and stakeholder reporting.

best_practices: Define the review scope before running any script or test workflow.
Use authorized test targets and document rules of engagement before penetration testing.
Validate findings manually before treating them as confirmed security defects.
anti_patterns: Do not run penetration tests against systems without written authorization.
Do not treat placeholder script output as a completed security assessment.
Do not copy environment files that contain real secrets into shared locations.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps structure security reviews, threat models, audit planning, authorized testing workflows, and cryptography reference work.

faq.question: Does it perform real penetration testing automatically?
faq.answer: No. The included script is a local placeholder workflow and needs user extension for real testing.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it access secrets?
faq.answer: No evidence was found that it reads or exfiltrates secrets. The setup example only copies an example environment file.

faq.question: What outputs can it create?
faq.answer: The scripts print terminal reports and can write JSON output when the user provides an output path.

faq.question: Is this enough for compliance approval?
faq.answer: No. Use it as review support, then validate results with qualified security and compliance reviewers.
